# macOS Inspector 1.4.2

This release tightens two decisions that matter during an investigation: whether an application trust check actually finished, and whether a process shown in a report is still the process about to receive a signal.

## Changes

- Application Trust now records an incomplete code-signature or Gatekeeper check as unknown when macOS returns an internal trust-service error. A separate file-permission or integrity concern remains visible even if a trust check did not finish. The dashboard names the missing check and lowers evidence confidence instead of implying that the app passed or failed it.
- A validly signed Apple system component that Gatekeeper says is not an independently assessable app is shown as **Gatekeeper not applicable**. That result is not a rejection and does not establish that the component is safe.
- Process response requires a Live Triage snapshot no older than 15 minutes. Immediately before sending a signal, macOS Inspector compares the current PID, owner, parent, executable path, and process start with the report. Old reports and snapshots without a start identity cannot authorize a process action.
- An isolated low-priority process signal, such as a path under a hidden user directory, stays in the technical evidence as context. It no longer creates a process-response finding on its own. Corroborated medium- and high-priority candidates still appear for review.

## Using this release

If an application card says a trust check did not finish, use **Recheck this app** before deciding whether to keep using the application. Review any separate permission or integrity warning on the same card; a missing trust result does not erase it.

If process-response controls say the snapshot is stale, run Live Triage again. Confirm the process is unexpected and preserve relevant evidence before terminating it. A process marked zombie has already exited; signaling it will not remove it.

## Boundaries

The collectors remain read-only. Process termination is a separate, explicitly confirmed action; the identity check narrows PID-reuse risk but cannot eliminate the race between verification and signaling. No application reputation database was added. Online intelligence remains opt-in and does not turn an indicator match or signature result into a malware verdict.

The portable package is not Apple-signed or notarized. Verify its checksum before opening the launcher. This release does not require administrator privileges or Full Disk Access for normal use, though protected evidence may remain unavailable.

## Install

Download `macos-inspector-1.4.2-macos.zip` and `SHA256SUMS` from this release. Run `shasum -a 256 macos-inspector-1.4.2-macos.zip` and compare the full digest with `SHA256SUMS`. Extract the ZIP, then double-click **macOS Inspector.command**.
